meaning.en: To meet face to face in a narrow lane, with no way to avoid each other — used of rivals.
meaning.zh: 在很窄的路上相遇，无处可让。多指仇人或对手相遇，难以相容。

equivalents: come face to face with a rival

examples.zh: 两支强队在决赛中狭路相逢。
examples.en: The two strong teams meet head-on in the final.

examples.zh: 狭路相逢勇者胜。
examples.en: When rivals meet head-on, the bravest wins.

story.en: The Han ballad opens with two carriages meeting in a lane so narrow that neither could pass.
story.zh: 《相逢行》：“相逢狭路间，道隘不容车。”

usage.en: Predicate; set phrase 狭路相逢勇者胜.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常说“狭路相逢勇者胜”。

meaning.en: More than enough; with plenty to spare.
meaning.zh: 形容房屋或钱财非常宽裕，用不完；也指能力足以胜任。

equivalents: more than up to the job

examples.zh: 这点钱买张火车票绰绰有余。
examples.en: This money is more than enough for a train ticket.

examples.zh: 以他的能力，管理这个部门绰绰有余。
examples.en: With his ability, he's more than up to running this department.

story.en: Mencius, holding no office, said that he was free to come and go: 'surely I have ample room to manoeuvre'.
story.zh: 《孟子》：“则吾进退，岂不绰绰然有余裕哉？”

meaning.en: War raging everywhere.
meaning.zh: 形容战争激烈，到处是炮火。

examples.zh: 在那战火纷飞的年代，他们失去了联系。
examples.en: In those war-torn years they lost touch with each other.

examples.zh: 记者冒着生命危险深入战火纷飞的前线。
examples.en: Reporters risked their lives to reach the front line where fighting raged.

usage.zh: 多作定语，常说“战火纷飞的年代”。

meaning.en: To gain both fame and money.
meaning.zh: 名誉和利益都得到了。

examples.zh: 这部小说让他名利双收。
examples.en: The novel brought him fame and fortune.

examples.zh: 很多年轻人梦想一夜之间名利双收。
examples.en: Many young people dream of becoming rich and famous overnight.

meaning.en: To think something over from every angle.
meaning.zh: 思考事情的前因后果，反复考虑。

examples.zh: 思前想后，我还是决定辞职。
examples.en: After thinking it over and over, I decided to quit.

examples.zh: 她一夜没睡，思前想后。
examples.en: She lay awake all night, turning it over in her mind.

usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用在作决定之前。

meaning.en: A public place with many people around.
meaning.zh: 聚集很多人的公开场合。

examples.zh: 在大庭广众之下大声喧哗很不礼貌。
examples.en: It's rude to make a racket in public.

examples.zh: 他在大庭广众面前向她求婚。
examples.en: He proposed to her in front of everyone.

usage.en: Usually 在大庭广众之下/面前.

meaning.en: Known to everybody.
meaning.zh: 每个人都知道。

examples.zh: 吸烟有害健康，这是人人皆知的道理。
examples.en: Everyone knows that smoking damages your health.

examples.zh: 这件事在村里早已人人皆知。
examples.en: The whole village has long known about it.

meaning.en: To give an answer that has nothing to do with the question.
meaning.zh: 回答的不是所问的问题。

examples.zh: 面对记者提问，发言人答非所问。
examples.en: Asked by reporters, the spokesperson dodged the question.

examples.zh: 考试时一定要审清题目，避免答非所问。
examples.en: Read exam questions carefully so your answer isn't off the point.

meaning.en: Brief, clear and to the point.
meaning.zh: 简单明了，抓住要点。

examples.zh: 请简明扼要地介绍一下你的项目。
examples.en: Please describe your project briefly and to the point.

examples.zh: 这份报告写得简明扼要。
examples.en: The report is concise and clear.

meaning.en: To accomplish nothing at all.
meaning.zh: 连一件事也没有做成。

equivalents: have nothing to show for it

examples.zh: 年过四十，他觉得自己一事无成。
examples.en: Past forty, he feels he has achieved nothing.

examples.zh: 光想不做，只会一事无成。
examples.en: All talk and no action gets you nowhere.

meaning.en: To look inferior by comparison.
meaning.zh: 互相比较之下，显出一方的不足。

examples.zh: 和新款手机相比，旧款明显相形见绌。
examples.en: Next to the new phone, the old model pales in comparison.

examples.zh: 在高手面前，我的水平相形见绌。
examples.en: Beside the experts, my skills don't hold a candle.

usage.en: Predicate; often 与/和…相比，相形见绌.

meaning.en: Huge, terrifying waves; great perils or upheavals.
meaning.zh: 汹涌吓人的浪涛。比喻险恶的环境或尖锐激烈的斗争。

examples.zh: 小船在惊涛骇浪中颠簸。
examples.en: The little boat was tossed about on the stormy sea.

examples.zh: 他经历过商海的惊涛骇浪，什么场面没见过？
examples.en: He's weathered the stormy seas of business — what hasn't he seen?

usage.en: Subject or object; often 在惊涛骇浪中.

meaning.en: Numb and indifferent; unmoved by others' suffering.
meaning.zh: 原指肢体麻痹，失去感觉；比喻对外界事物反应迟钝或漠不关心。

examples.zh: 面对别人的痛苦，他竟然麻木不仁。
examples.en: He was utterly callous in the face of others' suffering.

examples.zh: 长期看到这些新闻，人们变得麻木不仁。
examples.en: After years of such news, people have grown numb to it.

meaning.en: Wine cups and drinking tallies criss-crossing — a lively banquet.
meaning.zh: 酒杯和酒筹交互错杂。形容宴会热闹的场面。

examples.zh: 宴会上觥筹交错，宾主尽欢。
examples.en: Glasses clinked at the banquet and hosts and guests enjoyed themselves.

examples.zh: 年会上觥筹交错，热闹非凡。
examples.en: Drinks flowed freely and the company party was very lively.

story.en: Ouyang Xiu described his guests at a feast in the hills: cups and tallies crossing, people rising and sitting amid the noise.
story.zh: 《醉翁亭记》：“觥筹交错，起坐而喧哗者，众宾欢也。”

pinyin: fǎn qí dào ér xíng zhī
literal: reverse · its · way · and · do · it

meaning.en: To do the exact opposite of the usual or expected way.
meaning.zh: 采取跟对方或常规相反的办法去做。

examples.zh: 别人都在降价，他却反其道而行之，主打高端市场。
examples.en: While everyone else cut prices, he did the opposite and went upmarket.

examples.zh: 有时候反其道而行之，反而能出奇制胜。
examples.en: Sometimes going against the grain is what wins the day.

meaning.en: To die of old age at home; humorously, for things that finally come to an end.
meaning.zh: 原指年老在家中安然死去；现也比喻事物自然消亡。

examples.zh: 老人九十多岁寿终正寝。
examples.en: The old man died peacefully at home in his nineties.

examples.zh: 那台老电脑终于寿终正寝了。
examples.en: That old computer has finally given up the ghost.

usage.en: Predicate; humorous for objects or projects.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，用于事物时带诙谐色彩。

meaning.en: When eliminating evil, do it thoroughly.
meaning.zh: 清除坏人坏事必须彻底。

examples.zh: 打击犯罪团伙必须除恶务尽。
examples.en: Criminal gangs must be rooted out completely.

examples.zh: 整治腐败要除恶务尽，不留后患。
examples.en: Anti-corruption work must be thorough and leave no lingering threat.

usage.en: Predicate; formal, common in official language.

meaning.en: As fast as wind and lightning.
meaning.zh: 像风吹电闪一样。形容非常迅速。

examples.zh: 高铁风驰电掣般驶过。
examples.en: The high-speed train flashed past at lightning speed.

examples.zh: 一辆摩托车风驰电掣地冲了过去。
examples.en: A motorbike hurtled past like the wind.

usage.en: Adverbial (风驰电掣般/地) or predicate.

literal: not at all · not · avoid · saying

meaning.en: To speak frankly, without hiding anything.
meaning.zh: 一点也不隐讳，直截了当地说出来。

examples.zh: 他毫不讳言自己犯过的错误。
examples.en: He openly admits the mistakes he has made.

examples.zh: 教练毫不讳言，球队状态不佳。
examples.en: The coach said frankly that the team was out of form.

meaning.en: To come into being and die out on its own, without anyone's help or interference.
meaning.zh: 自然地发生，自然地消灭。指任其自然发展，不加过问。

examples.zh: 这些小企业得不到扶持，只能自生自灭。
examples.en: Without support, these small firms are left to sink or swim.

examples.zh: 不能对流浪动物放任其自生自灭。
examples.en: We can't leave stray animals to fend for themselves.

usage.en: Predicate; often 任其/听任自生自灭.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常说“任其自生自灭”。

meaning.en: Orderly and methodical, like music keeping perfect time.
meaning.zh: 比喻言语行动有条理，有分寸。

examples.zh: 这孩子说话有板有眼，像个小大人。
examples.en: The child speaks in such an orderly way, like a little adult.

examples.zh: 他做事有板有眼，从不马虎。
examples.en: He's methodical in everything and never sloppy.

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial. 板/眼 are the strong and weak beats in Chinese opera.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语。板、眼原指戏曲音乐的节拍。

meaning.en: To talk in a lively, witty and wide-ranging way.
meaning.zh: 形容谈论广泛而又生动。

examples.zh: 他学识渊博，在座谈会上议论风生。
examples.en: Being very learned, he held forth brilliantly at the forum.

examples.zh: 饭桌上大家议论风生，十分热闹。
examples.en: Conversation round the dinner table was lively and animated.

meaning.en: Isolated and without any help.
meaning.zh: 处境孤立，得不到援助。

equivalents: with no one to turn to

examples.zh: 在国外遇到困难时，她感到孤立无援。
examples.en: When she ran into trouble abroad she felt she had no one to turn to.

examples.zh: 这个提案在会上孤立无援，最终被否决。
examples.en: The proposal found no support at the meeting and was voted down.

meaning.en: To be in league with one another for bad purposes.
meaning.zh: 比喻臭味相投的人勾结在一起。

examples.zh: 这些官员与开发商沆瀣一气，侵吞公款。
examples.en: These officials were in cahoots with developers and embezzled public money.

examples.zh: 他们沆瀣一气，联手打压竞争对手。
examples.en: They're hand in glove, ganging up to crush their rivals.

story.en: In the Tang, examiner Cui Hang passed a candidate named Cui Xie; people joked that examiner and graduate were 'Hang and Xie in one breath' (沆瀣 means night mist).
story.zh: 《南部新书》：崔沆主试，取崔瀣，时人嘲之曰：“座主门生，沆瀣一气。”
